mission: Cinderline begins the prison snatch under false procedural cover. Lysa manipulates systems; Talon reads the pattern before Ben can. The first snatch team breaches the wing. Ben breaks cover and saves Talon physically, disabling rather than killing and protecting confused prison staff. His restraint is active, not passive — he chooses non-lethal Force work and lightsaber control even when speed would be easier.
why_now: Chapter 7 occupies the setup phase and carries the next locked outline turn.
conflict: Ben should look heroic here. The later moral danger works better if the reader first sees that his instincts are genuinely protective. Talon’s growing recognition that Ben is good at this, even constrained, should land underneath his complaints.
turning_point: Ben can win the fight, but Talon says they are going the wrong way.
closing_hook: Ben can win the fight, but Talon says they are going the wrong way.
setting: Tarn Velos prison interior — the visitor wing corridor, then the cell block as Cinderline begins the snatch under false procedural cover. Storm-lit from outside through narrow slit windows; emergency strips along the floor; the prison alarm pitch goes wrong before any visible threat appears. Lockdown protocols cycle in the background.
emotional_trajectory: Ben should look heroic here. The later moral danger works better if the reader first sees that his instincts are genuinely protective. Talon’s growing recognition that Ben is good at this, even constrained, should land underneath his complaints.
